title: SDK request routing playbook and enterprise onboarding heuristics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We receive a high volume of non-bug SDK requests from customers and internal stakeholders that vary along three axes: language support, authentication patterns, and streaming ergonomics. Without a clear routing and prioritization playbook we waste PM/Eng/Design cycles re-triaging similar asks and miss enterprise onboarding SLAs.

Goal: Produce a lightweight, operational 'routing playbook' that triages incoming SDK/client library requests into one of four buckets: self-serve backlog, roadmap candidate, enterprise fast-path, or security/legal review. The playbook should be explicit about signals (customer tier, active P0 impact, integration blockers, regulatory requirements), required artifacts for escalation, and SLA targets for enterprise requests.

Scope: Focused on non-bug requests related to SDKs and client libraries: 1) new language client requests (e.g. Rust, Go, .NET idioms), 2) auth patterns (token rotation, SSO flows, machine credential patterns), and 3) streaming ergonomics (chunked streaming APIs, reconnection semantics, cancellation, typed streaming in strongly-typed languages). Does not include packaging infra work (CI pipelines) or open-source governance exceptions.

Acceptance criteria:
- A one-page playbook (Confluence) with decision tree and required intake fields.
- Updated intake form template for support/CS that enforces necessary metadata (customer tier, integration deadline, security constraints, minimal repro).
- Clear routing rules surfaced in triage queue and a Slack workflow to notify engineering owners for enterprise fast-path cases.
- Pilot routing on 10 incoming requests and measure routing accuracy and SLA compliance.

Success metrics (first 8 weeks):
- Median time-to-first-response for enterprise-sdk requests <= 48 hours.
- >= 80% of enterprise requests contain required artifacts on first submission.
- Reduction in PM re-triage time by 40% (tracked via time-logged tags).

Proposed heuristics (short):
- Language requests: route to backlog unless there is an active contract or >5 customers requesting a specific language within a quarter; otherwise mark as roadmap candidate. For enterprise customers with contractual need, escalate to enterprise fast-path.
- Auth changes: any request that touches token rotation, KMS/HSM, or SSO must include security_review_required and automatically create an ENG security spike ticket.
- Streaming ergonomics: if request impacts live connection behavior (reconnect, backpressure, binary frames) and customer is on Dedicated/Private, escalate to eng owner and design for an SDK ergonomic proposal.

Operational playbook highlights:
- Intake fields: customer name, customer tier, use-case summary, deadline, reproducible snippet, desired language/feature, regulatory flags, repo/PR link if internal proof-of-concept exists.
- Owner matrix: PM -> triage lead (rotation), ENG -> SDK owner (per language), Design -> API ergonomics consult for streaming/typed APIs, Security -> auto-notify for auth/regulatory flags.
- Escalation artifacts: business justification (~250 words), customer impact evidence, test harness or sample app, and suggested prioritization (can we ship a shim or sample vs full client lib?).

Notes on trade-offs:
- Lean playbook prioritizes speed over exhaustiveness; we accept occasional false positives in enterprise fast-path to avoid missing critical customers.
- We will prefer short-term bridging shims or adapter patterns where full language client implementations are high-cost.

Links and artifacts: [Confluence playbook draft](https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SDK/pages/SDK+Routing+Playbook+Draft), [Intake form prototype](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SDK-Intake-Prototype), GitHub backlog label: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues?q=is%3Aissue+label%3Asdk-request, Slack channel: #sdk-triage.

Next steps (owned):
- Draft Confluence one-pager and intake template (Aisha) — due 2025-02-17.
- Sync with Security and Eng SDK leads to validate automatic routing rules (Marco) — sync scheduled 2025-02-20.
- Pilot triage for two weeks on support queue and collect metrics (triage rotation) — pilot 2025-02-24 to 2025-03-10.
- Review pilot results and iterate on playbook (PM+Eng) — review 2025-03-12.
